name: Destroyer
label: Merge
lede: Dan Bejar named his band Destroyer in Vancouver in 1995, not knowing Kiss had an album by that name. Fourteen albums later he's still writing the wordiest songs on Merge, and the saxophones showed up around 2011.

eras.title: A rock name nobody had taken
eras.text: Dan Bejar started Destroyer alone in Vancouver with a four-track and a head full of words. Within six years he'd gone from deliberately out-of-tune home tapes to a real band, a real studio and a second job writing the oddest songs on The New Pornographers' records.

q: I was kind of blown away that it hadn't been taken already.
years.h: A Vancouver dropout starts Destroyer, unaware Kiss got there first
years.p: Dan Bejar, who left the University of British Columbia after mostly English and philosophy, starts recording alone as Destroyer. He picked the name because it sounded like rock and roll.
years.xp:
Bejar was born in Vancouver in 1972 to a Spanish physicist father and an American mother who taught Spanish.

Only later did he learn that Kiss had a 1976 album called Destroyer. He told an interviewer in 2008 he'd been too out of it to know.

years.h: We'll Build Them a Golden Bridge arrives, out of tune on purpose
years.p: Destroyer's debut is sixteen lo-fi home recordings with the guitars left untuned. One of them, The Pornographers, later helps name a band.
years.xp: Reviewers heard a real gift for melody under the deliberate murk. The song title stuck with A.C. Newman, who cited it among the sources when he named [[The New Pornographers|25b75a66-ce83-4db3-b136-395a3c3784c4]].

years.h: A.C. Newman recruits Bejar, Neko Case and John Collins
years.p: The Vancouver side project is [[The New Pornographers|25b75a66-ce83-4db3-b136-395a3c3784c4]], and Dan Bejar's songs become its wild card.
years.xp: Bejar's Breakin' the Law was a Destroyer song before it landed on the New Pornographers' debut, Mass Romantic, in November 2000.

years.h: John Collins brings Destroyer into a real studio
years.p: Producer and bassist [[John Collins|17fe13d1-ca12-4e28-a7d5-0deb9f631650]] joins for City of Daughters, the first Destroyer record made in a proper studio. Drummer Scott Morgan, later known as [[Loscil|4f2c565b-ac40-4678-ba61-4fcf3b97edbc]], arrives around the same time.
years.xp:
Pitchfork later spotted the wordiness that would become Dan Bejar's trademark here, while noting that not every line rewarded close reading.

Scott Morgan played drums, saxophone, clarinet and classical guitar in Destroyer from 1998 to 2002 and came back from 2005 to 2007.

years.h: Two months after Mass Romantic, Bejar is in Spain
years.p: A.C. Newman later joked that Dan Bejar moved to Spain two months after the New Pornographers' debut came out, which is one reason Bejar was always a part-time Pornographer.

years.h: Streethawk: A Seduction ends the run Bejar had in mind
years.p: After Thief (2000) brought in a full band, Dan Bejar said he hoped City of Daughters, Thief and Streethawk would play as one progression. Pitchfork later gave it a 9.1.

eras.title: A different costume every record
eras.text: Destroyer kept changing clothes: a loose live-in-the-room record, an album built almost entirely from MIDI, then a warm full-band record that turned a nine-minute song into a singalong. Merge became the home base in the US, and a steady Vancouver crew formed around Bejar.

years.h: This Night, loose and under-rehearsed, comes out on Merge
years.p: Cut with little studio time, it split critics between beautiful mess and plain mess. By 2006 Dan Bejar called it his favorite Destroyer record.

years.h: Nearly every backing part on Your Blues is MIDI
years.p: Dan Bejar called the sound European blues.
years.xp: The follow-up EP, Notorious Lightning & Other Works, redid six of the songs with a live band: Victoria's [[Frog Eyes|9cf2cd10-7629-488b-abc2-f9cca721383a]], led by [[Carey Mercer|bb3ec24e-b97f-446e-b397-1f5d926f30a1]].

years.h: European Oils becomes the song the room sings back
years.p: Destroyer's Rubies is the seventh album in six years and puts the band up front: Ted Bois on piano, Nicolas Bragg on guitar, Scott Morgan on drums. Live, the nine-minute song became a cathartic peak Dan Bejar never planned.
years.xp:
Bejar told Pitchfork he'd never hit fewer notes, yet thought Rubies had the best set of vocals he'd recorded. He called the production warm, lush and focused on making the band sound good.

The vinyl carries an extra track called Loscil's Rubies, a nod to drummer Scott Morgan's ambient project.

years.h: Bejar joins Carey Mercer and Spencer Krug in Swan Lake
years.p: The trio pairs Dan Bejar with [[Carey Mercer|bb3ec24e-b97f-446e-b397-1f5d926f30a1]] of [[Frog Eyes|9cf2cd10-7629-488b-abc2-f9cca721383a]] and [[Spencer Krug|2ba12d30-216e-48b2-b673-e92203bab01c]] of [[Wolf Parade|b7ddce8b-9e5c-46bd-9d33-41b134ce1a7f]] and Sunset Rubdown. Two albums follow, in 2006 and 2009.

years.h: Bejar walks into Trouble in Dreams short on ideas
years.p: He admitted to a scary lack of them. Ted Bois answered with string and synth arrangements instead of plain keyboard parts.

eras.title: The year the guitars left
eras.text: Recorded slowly over two years at John Collins and David Carswell's JC/DC Studios, Kaputt swapped guitars for trumpet, saxophone and female backing vocals. It was the record that finally put Destroyer in front of people who'd never heard of Destroyer.

years.h: On Archer on the Beach, Bejar talks over Loscil
years.p: The EP pairs Dan Bejar with ambient producers [[Tim Hecker|c7ee3bc9-780c-42c0-91e9-4cd70ad692d3]] and [[Loscil|4f2c565b-ac40-4678-ba61-4fcf3b97edbc]]. The spoken-word Grief Point runs over Loscil's music.

years.h: Kaputt trades guitars for trumpet and sax
years.p: Released on Merge and Dead Oceans, it adds JP Carter's trumpet, Joseph Shabason's saxophone and Sibel Thrasher's vocals. Visual artist Kara Walker co-wrote Suicide Demo for Kara Walker.
years.xp:
Dan Bejar said he sang in a completely different way here, almost like speaking into a vacuum. It was also the first Destroyer album with female backing vocals.

The Guardian's Alexis Petridis called it an open love letter to a vanished pop era. Pitchfork ranked it the second-best album of 2011, and it made the Polaris Music Prize shortlist.

years.h: Late Night with Jimmy Fallon gives Destroyer its first network TV spot
years.p: Kaputt also brings an official music video and a tour on which Dan Bejar sings without an instrument.

years.big: "The English language seemed spent, despicable, not easily singable."
years.h: Five Spanish Songs is five Sr. Chinarro covers, all in Spanish
years.p: Dan Bejar's line in the EP's press release. The songs come from the Spanish songwriter Antonio Luque's band.
years.xp: The press release opened with Dan Bejar declaring the English language worn out and not easily singable. Spanish was his father's language; Bejar had lived in Spain in the early 2000s.

eras.title: Bigger than a side gig
eras.text: Dan Bejar quietly stepped back from The New Pornographers after Brill Bruisers in 2014, and Destroyer grew to fill the room: strings first, then a Thatcher-era chill.

years.cap: Destroyer at the Commodore Ballroom, Vancouver, October 17, 2015
years.h: Destroyer cuts Poison Season live, strings and all
years.p: A live band and big string sections. Dan Bejar said it was the first record that came close to how he saw himself as a singer.
years.xp: Bejar also said he couldn't have made something this ambitious without the success of Kaputt.

years.h: Whiteout Conditions arrives without Bejar
years.p: Dan Bejar, who stopped touring with the New Pornographers after 2014's Brill Bruisers, told Exclaim! he was deep in Destroyer's next album and didn't hear New Pornographers songs in it.

years.h: ken takes its name from a Suede working title
years.p: It's the original working title of Suede's The Wild Ones. Drummer Joshua Wells, also of [[Black Mountain|4898b9ad-f564-4ff1-9046-b1a16dfd5200]], produced the record.
years.xp: Dan Bejar described the record to Exclaim! as cold and stark, colored by Britain in the Thatcher years that he'd been reading and thinking about.

eras.title: Still boogieing
eras.text: Past fifty, Bejar made peace with his old band and kept Destroyer moving, the lineup around him steady for more than a decade. The records got stranger and the reviews stayed kind.

years.h: Bejar is back in the New Pornographers, on tour
years.p: The band announces tours playing Mass Romantic and Twin Cinema in full with Dan Bejar, his first shows with them in seven years.
years.xp: A.C. Newman joked that Bejar was coming and God knows if they'd get him again.

years.cap: Dan Bejar at Amsterdam Bar and Hall, St. Paul, Minnesota, June 5, 2022
years.h: Labyrinthitis brings synths, dance beats and a Polaris shortlist
years.p: Destroyer's thirteenth album leans on both and lands on the Polaris Music Prize shortlist.

years.cap: Dan Bejar at Amsterdam Bar and Hall, St. Paul, Minnesota
years.h: Thirty years in, Dan's Boogie draws an 8.0 from Pitchfork
years.p: Destroyer's fourteenth album also makes the Polaris Music Prize longlist.
